## Source: benchmark/baseline.md
# External baseline contract (before B01)

The interface is a subprocess CLI run from an isolated working directory.
Commands print exactly one JSON value to stdout on success (exit 0); expected
application failures print `{"error":"CODE"}` to stderr (exit 1). Commands
persist across separate processes in `tasks.json` in that directory. `list`
on missing storage returns `[]` without creating the file.

Each task result has exactly `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`,
`created_at`, and `due_date`. IDs are unique nonempty strings; timestamps are
UTC ISO strings ending in `Z`. Lists sort by `(created_at, id)` ascending.

* `create --title T --description D [--priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH]
  [--due-date UTC_TIMESTAMP]`: nonblank title, verbatim description, new ID,
  status `pending`, priority default `NORMAL`, current creation timestamp,
  due date default `null`. Blank title fails `invalid_title`; malformed or
  non-UTC due date fails `invalid_due_date` without changing storage.
* `list`: return all tasks including completed tasks.
* `list-high`: return only HIGH tasks (including completed ones).
* `list-overdue`: return only pending tasks with a non-null due date **strictly
  earlier** than current UTC time. Undated and completed tasks are excluded.
* `complete --id ID`: pending task becomes completed and is persisted; a
  missing ID fails `task_not_found`, an already completed task fails
  `invalid_transition`, both without altering the stored file.
* `delete --id ID`: remove and return the task (pending or completed); missing
  ID fails `task_not_found` without altering storage.
* `migrate`: explicit conversion of legacy unversioned records to version 3
  (add `priority: NORMAL`, `due_date: null`) and version 2 records to version 3
  (add `due_date: null`); return `{"migrated": N}`. Running on current data or
  absent storage returns `{"migrated": 0}`. Legacy reads fail
  `migration_required` without changing data. New writes use a version-3
  envelope with `schema_version` and `records`.

Malformed JSON and invalid record shape, duplicate IDs, blank IDs/titles,
invalid enums and timestamps fail `invalid_state` on read. Failed operations
must not mutate persisted bytes. An exact-time overdue boundary can be checked
only with a controlled clock; the external CLI oracle checks widely separated
past and future instants instead of relying on timing-sensitive sleeps.

The oracle exercises *both* executable CLIs with fresh subprocesses and
independent temporary directories; it asserts this contract before comparing
normalized outcomes. Random IDs and wall-clock timestamps are checked for
properties, not falsely required to be byte-identical across tracks.

## Source: benchmark/requirements/B10.md
# B10 — Optional owner (cross-cutting)

Add `create --owner USER_ID` and a returned `owner` string. Omitted owner and
migrated tasks have `""`. A supplied owner is trimmed and must be nonblank;
otherwise fail `invalid_owner`. Add `list-owner --owner USER_ID` for exact,
case-sensitive matches (including `""` for unowned). This step does not yet
require that an owner correspond to a user.


## Source: benchmark/requirements/B01.md
# B01 — Critical priority (local)

Add `CRITICAL` above `HIGH` to accepted task priorities. `create --priority
CRITICAL` persists and returns that value; `list` includes it. `list-high`
continues to mean exactly `HIGH`. Existing LOW, NORMAL and HIGH tasks retain
their values through migration. A missing priority still defaults to NORMAL.


## Source: benchmark/requirements/B02.md
# B02 — Task tags (local)

Accept zero or more `--tag VALUE` flags on `create`. Each VALUE must be a
nonblank string after trimming whitespace; store the trimmed value. Tags are
case-sensitive, deduplicated while retaining first occurrence order, and
returned as a `tags` array on every task. Omission and migrated older tasks
have `tags: []`. Empty tag input fails `invalid_tag` with no new task.


## Source: benchmark/requirements/B03.md
# B03 — List by tag (local)

Add `list-tag --tag VALUE`. Return tasks whose `tags` contains exactly VALUE
(case-sensitive; query input is not trimmed), including completed tasks, in
normal order. Reject blank or whitespace-only query input with `invalid_tag`.
A tag not present returns `[]`; the query never changes storage. For example,
`work` does not select a task tagged `Work`.


## Source: benchmark/requirements/B04.md
# B04 — Source label (local)

Add optional `create --source VALUE` and a returned `source` string on every
task. Preserve the supplied value verbatim, including whitespace; omission
and migrated tasks use `""`. Listing and subsequent mutations preserve it.
This is a small field addition: creation timestamps already exist at baseline.


## Source: benchmark/requirements/B05.md
# B05 — Status filter (local)

Add `list-status --status pending|completed`. Return precisely the tasks in
the requested status in normal order. An empty result is `[]`; querying does
not change storage. Both values include all matching tasks at this step.


## Source: benchmark/requirements/B06.md
# B06 — Categories (cross-cutting)

Add `create --category VALUE`, default `""`, returned on all tasks. A supplied
nonempty value is trimmed; whitespace-only input fails `invalid_category`.
Omission, an explicitly empty value, and migrated tasks use `""`. Add
`list-category --category VALUE` for exact, case-sensitive matching, including
`""` to select uncategorized tasks. Standard list retains all tasks.


## Source: benchmark/requirements/B07.md
# B07 — Appendable notes (cross-cutting)

Tasks gain `notes`, an ordered array of strings, initially `[]` (including
migrated tasks). `append-note --id ID --text TEXT` appends trimmed nonblank
TEXT and returns the updated task. Blank text fails `invalid_note`; failed
appends do not alter the task. Repeated appends preserve insertion order.


## Source: benchmark/requirements/B08.md
# B08 — Archival (cross-cutting)

Tasks gain an `archived` boolean, default false (also for migrated tasks),
independent of pending/completed status. `archive --id ID` sets true and
returns the task; repeating it fails `invalid_transition`. Archived tasks are
hidden from `list`, `list-high`, `list-overdue`, `list-tag`, `list-status`, and
`list-category`. Add `list-archived` to expose them in normal order. Archiving
either pending or completed tasks is valid; the status value does not change.


## Source: benchmark/requirements/B09.md
# B09 — Due window (cross-cutting)

Add `list-due --start UTC_TIMESTAMP --end UTC_TIMESTAMP`. Include only
nonarchived pending tasks with a due date in the **inclusive** interval
`[start, end]`, ordered normally. Equal endpoints are valid; start after end
fails `invalid_window`. Invalid/non-UTC timestamps fail `invalid_due_date`.
Undated or completed tasks are excluded and the query has no write effect.

returns the task; repeating it fails `invalid_transition`. Archived tasks are
hidden from `list`, `list-high`, `list-overdue`, `list-tag`, `list-status`, and
`list-category`. Add `list-archived` to expose them in normal order. Archiving
either pending or completed tasks is valid; the status value does not change.

# B09 — Due window (cross-cutting)

Add `list-due --start UTC_TIMESTAMP --end UTC_TIMESTAMP`. Include only
nonarchived pending tasks with a due date in the **inclusive** interval
`[start, end]`, ordered normally. Equal endpoints are valid; start after end
fails `invalid_window`. Invalid/non-UTC timestamps fail `invalid_due_date`.
Undated or completed tasks are excluded and the query has no write effect.
